provider: Interrail Global Pass (Youth, 2nd class)
ageRange: 12-27 (age on the first day of the trip)
cost: Youth 2nd class 2026, Flexi: 4 days in 1 month EUR 212; 5 days in 1 month EUR 239; 7 days in 1 month EUR 286; 10 days in 2 months EUR 335; 15 days in 2 months EUR 415 (adult 2nd class EUR 283 / 318 / 381 / 447 / 553). Sold in Norway by Entur at NOK 2,527 / 2,824 / 3,341 for 4 / 5 / 7 days (list valid from 13 Aug 2026, includes a NOK 195 booking fee at Entur counters and phone). Cost per travel day: EUR 53 (4-day), EUR 48 (5-day), EUR 41 (7-day).
benefit: Unlimited trains on the chosen number of travel days (midnight to midnight) in 33 countries, 2nd class; the youth price is 25% below the adult price. Participating operators in Norway: Vy, SJ Norge, Go-Ahead Nordic (SJ Norge regional trains Oslo-Dombas-Trondheim, about 6h40, are covered; SJ Norge night trains Oslo-Trondheim need a reserved seat or bed). The pass can be started up to 11 months after purchase.
typicalSaving: EUR 71 below the adult 4-day price (EUR 212 vs EUR 283). Versus point-to-point tickets for 2-3 intercity legs the pass is normally the more expensive option (see worthItForThisTrip).
howToGet: Buy at interrail.eu (mobile or paper pass, set Norway as country of residence) or in Norway through Entur customer service (tel. 61 27 90 88), staffed stations or europarundt.no; have the passport number ready. Seat reservations for high-speed and night trains are booked separately.
conditions: Age is judged on the date the trip starts. A 2nd class pass is valid in 2nd class only. High-speed and night trains need paid reservations that the pass does not include (a Global Plus Pass that covers reservations exists, price not retrieved). Home-country rule for Norwegian residents: the pass covers only one outbound and one inbound journey inside Norway (Vy: each completed within one day; Northern Norway destinations up to two travel days per direction); Interrail community answers and Seat61 say these use normal travel days, the official FAQ page does not state it; they may be used to reach a home airport. Norwegians cannot buy the Norway One Country Pass. Indicative reservation fees from Interrail's official fee pages (2nd class, pass holders): Germany ICE/IC/EC optional EUR 5.50; Austria Railjet optional EUR 3; Czechia IC/EC/RJ EUR 3.60 (mandatory only on a few IC trains), RegioJet mandatory EUR 1.30-2.80; Poland EIP mandatory EUR 10, EIC/IC/TLK EUR 0.70 recommended, EuroCity to Poland mandatory EUR 3-5.50; Hungary IC mandatory EUR 1.70-2.60; Italy Frecciarossa/Frecciargento mandatory EUR 13, Intercity EUR 3; Spain AVE and iryo EUR 10, Alvia/Intercity EUR 6.50, Avant EUR 4; France TGV INOUI EUR 10-20, Paris-Barcelona TGV EUR 35, Paris-Milan TGV EUR 31; Eurostar EUR 22-35; Norway SJ Norge regional Standard EUR 4.30 and Vy Standard EUR 6 (optional but advised). Night trains: Nightjet seat EUR 4.90-24.90, 6-bed couchette EUR 19.90-64.90, 4-bed couchette EUR 29.90-94.90 (dynamic prices, status June 2026).
worthItForThisTrip: Probably not for 2-3 intercity legs: a 4-day youth pass (EUR 212, about EUR 53 per travel day before reservations) only wins if each leg would cost more than roughly EUR 70 (3 legs) or EUR 105 (2 legs) as a ticket, which is rare in December when advance fares are cheap, unless a winter sale (25% off ran 25 Nov-17 Dec 2025) cuts it to about EUR 159 and the legs are long high-speed ones in France, Italy or Spain.
notes: interrail.com pages load prices dynamically, so the EUR table could not be read from the official page itself. The 4/5/7-day youth prices are cross-checked four ways: Seat61 (third-party fallback, EUR 212/239/286), DB international page ('from EUR 212'), SBB (official seller, CHF 202/228/272 valid from 1 Jan 2026) and Entur's NOK list (as quoted in a search result; the Entur page itself is JavaScript-rendered; NOK = EUR x 11 + 195 fee reproduces 2,527 / 2,824 / 3,341 exactly). 10- and 15-day prices are from Seat61 only. Benchmarks for point-to-point fares seen in sources: DB Sparpreis Young from EUR 16.99, Trenitalia FrecciaYOUNG EUR 19/29/39, Seat61 examples Prague-Berlin from EUR 18.99, Berlin-Amsterdam from EUR 37.99, Vienna-Bratislava about EUR 12. Sale history (Interrail promo terms page): 'Journeys that make a difference' 25% off all Global and One Country Passes excl. Plus, 25 Nov-17 Dec 2025; 'September Promo 2026' 24 Sep-1 Oct 2026 (ended) gave 50% off 1-3 month continuous Global Passes and 15% off Flexi, shorter and One Country Passes. A winter 2026 sale is plausible but not announced. Five friends on a 4-day pass = EUR 1,060 at list price. The Interrail Pass-benefits portal (hostel and city-card offers) sits behind a dynamic page and was not verified.

provider: Interrail One Country Pass / German Rail Pass (Youth, 2nd class)
ageRange: 12-27 (age on the first day of the trip)
cost: Valid as of 1 June 2026, youth 2nd class, 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 8 travel days within 1 month: Austria and Italy EUR 124 / 147 / 167 / 185 / 219; Spain EUR 145 / 167 / 188 / 206 / 239; Czechia EUR 79 / 97 / 114 / 131 / 162; Poland EUR 50 / 63 / 75 / 89 / 113. Germany (German Rail Pass) 3 / 4 / 5 / 7 / 10 / 15 days within 1 month: EUR 167 / 191 / 211 / 245 / 305 / 380 (CFR Calatori sales price list; SBB lists CHF 159 / 182 / 201 / 233 / 290 / 361). Adult 2nd class for 3 days, for comparison: Austria and Italy EUR 165, Spain EUR 193, Czechia EUR 105, Poland EUR 67, Germany EUR 223.
benefit: Unlimited trains inside ONE country on 3-8 travel days within a month (Germany: 3-15 days), 25% below the adult price for under-28s; can be cheaper than the Global Pass when all legs are in one country.
typicalSaving: Cost per travel day on the 3-day youth pass: Poland EUR 17, Czechia EUR 26, Austria and Italy EUR 41, Spain EUR 48, Germany EUR 56 (reservations extra).
howToGet: Order at interrail.eu or at a national seller (DB, SBB, CFR Calatori, Entur) with Norway as country of residence.
conditions: Not sold for the country where you live (a Norwegian can buy any country except Norway). Valid only in that country (the German Rail Pass cannot be used to travel to or from Germany); a 2nd class pass is valid in 2nd class only. Local and regional trains usually need no reservation; high-speed, international and night trains need a paid reservation (Italy Frecciarossa/Frecciargento EUR 13 mandatory; Italo is not among the Italian trains on Interrail's fee page). Promo passes can have different validity terms.
worthItForThisTrip: Probably not: only Poland (EUR 50 for 3 days) and Czechia (EUR 79 for 3 days) are cheap enough to beat full-price tickets, while the Italy, Austria, Spain and Germany passes (EUR 124-167 for 3 days plus reservations) lose to advance or youth fares such as FrecciaYOUNG (EUR 19-39), Sparpreis Young (from EUR 16.99) or Sparschiene (from EUR 9.90) whenever those are available.
notes: Austria, Italy, Spain, Czechia and Poland come from DB's official price list (PDF 'valid as of 01 June 2026'; the table layout was jumbled when extracted, but it matches the CFR list row for row). Germany is not in DB's PDF; its EUR figures come from CFR Calatori (an Interrail seller) and are corroborated only by SBB's CHF list, so treat Germany as medium confidence. The Interrail country pages load prices dynamically and could not be read. The December 2025 sale also covered One Country Passes (25% off, excl. Plus and Switzerland).

provider: SJ Norge - student discount (Trondheim-Oslo etc.)
ageRange: under 30 (students, apprentices, pupils)
benefit: 50% off the Standard Flexible fare for full-time students; accepted proof is any Norwegian student ID, or ISIC for international students, physical or digital. SJ Norge operates Oslo-Dombas-Trondheim.
typicalSaving: 50% off Standard Flexible; the page lists no student discount for Premium and says nothing about cheaper saver fares.
howToGet: Book on sj.no or the SJ app and choose the student passenger type; carry student ID (or ISIC) on board.
conditions: Proof must be shown on request (student ID, apprentice proof or proof of a paid semester fee). Under-26 youth fares do not exist at SJ Norge (only 6-17: 75% off Standard Flexible, 25% off Premium Flexible).
worthItForThisTrip: Only relevant if they take the train from Trondheim to Oslo or Gardermoen instead of flying direct, and then only after checking that the 50% flexible fare beats the plain saver fare.
notes: Fare prices for Trondheim-Oslo were not retrieved; listed because the brief asked for Norwegian domestic rail.

provider: Vy (Norway) - student discount
ageRange: under 30
benefit: 50% off single tickets (Flex Refunderbar) and the 30-day period ticket for students; 10% off Pluss, PlussNatt and Sove Refunderbar (minimum prices NOK 349 / 579 / 450). No student discount on Lavpris, the non-refundable Flex/Pluss/PlussNatt/Sove fares or the 7-day period ticket.
typicalSaving: Up to 50% on the discounted fare types; minimum prices apply regardless of the percentage.
howToGet: Book on vy.no or the Vy app with the student ticket type; carry student proof and photo ID.
conditions: Buy or activate the ticket before turning 30; tickets are only valid with approved ID. Proof: student ID or certificate with a valid semester sticker (photo ID too if the card has no photo), a school attestation for the current semester plus photo ID, or an ISIC issued by Kilroy; ANSA cards do not qualify. Foreign students are OK with confirmation of a paid semester fee. Not valid inside regional fare zones where local rules apply (Ruter Oslo/Akershus, Skyss Bergen, AtB Trondheim region, Kolumbus); SJ Norge and Go-Ahead follow their own rules. From 1 July 2026 apprentices under 30 also qualify.
worthItForThisTrip: Relevant only for domestic Norwegian legs such as Trondheim to Oslo Gardermoen; Lavpris saver fares get no student discount, so compare prices before relying on it.
notes: The Studentbevis app is not mentioned on the Vy train discount page (it is on the bus page). Search summaries disagree slightly on the range 10-50%; the page itself lists the per-fare percentages used here.

provider: SJ (Sweden) - youth and student discount
ageRange: 16-25 for the youth discount (up to and including 25); students with an accepted card at any age
benefit: 15% off the ticket price (2nd class, 2nd class Calm and selected travel cards) for ages 16-25 and for students; cheaper Last Minute tickets for under-26s, students and seniors, available shortly before departure.
typicalSaving: 15% off ordinary fares; Last Minute savings not quantified.
howToGet: Choose the youth or student passenger type on sj.se or the SJ app.
conditions: Valid ID must be shown to the train attendant: all passports, Swedish ID documents, Swedish migration agency cards and national ID cards from within the EU are accepted, other foreign IDs are not. A 23-year-old qualifies by age, so no student card is needed; students may instead show a Mecenat or STUK/Studentkortet card with the SJ logo, or an ISIC.
worthItForThisTrip: Only if the route touches Sweden (e.g. Gothenburg or Stockholm); passport as ID is enough for the 15% youth rate.
notes: sj.se pages are JavaScript-rendered and returned empty to the fetch tool, so the details come from search results quoting those three sj.se pages (one snippet looked dated). Whether the 15% applies to all fare types was inconsistent between snippets; confirm at booking.

provider: DSB (Denmark) - Ungdomsbillet and youth Orange fares
benefit: Ungdomsbillet: 30% off for ages 16-25 on trips across the Great Belt (Storebaelt) and on Funen and/or in Jutland (North Jutland excluded). Orange (cheap advance) tickets are also priced lower for ages 16-25 and SU-eligible students.
typicalSaving: 30% off eligible trips (e.g. Copenhagen-Aarhus is not named on the page but crosses the Great Belt).
howToGet: Buy on dsb.dk, in the DSB app, at ticket machines or at 7-Eleven at the station; choose the Ungdomsbillet / youth passenger category.
conditions: Valid ID is required (driving licence, health insurance card or passport) and the ticket is for a specific date and route; trips only within Zealand/Copenhagen are not listed as covered; Orange campaign fares such as 'Rejs til max 99' get no extra youth discount. The DSB pages do not say whether non-Danish residents qualify (the rule is age-based).
worthItForThisTrip: Useful only if Copenhagen-Odense-Aarhus style legs are on the plan; otherwise irrelevant.
notes: The Ungdomskort (monthly youth card) needs Danish education or residence and is irrelevant for visitors. Foreign-visitor eligibility for Ungdomsbillet is not stated on DSB's pages.

provider: Deutsche Bahn - Sparpreis Young / Super Sparpreis Young (under 27)
ageRange: up to and including 26 (age on the first travel day, checked on the train)
benefit: Cheap saver fares for under-27s on ICE and IC/EC within Germany: Sparpreis Young from EUR 16.99 (2nd class, one way); Super Sparpreis Young advertised from EUR 4.99 on 2026-10-11 (an earlier snapshot of the page showed EUR 12.99, so the low price may be a temporary campaign). BahnCard 25/50 holders get a further 25% (not on the City-Ticket).
howToGet: Book on bahn.de or in DB Navigator and choose the under-27 passenger category; no card needed.
conditions: Valid only within Germany and only on the booked ICE/IC/EC connection (regional trains allowed for the trip to or from the station if the journey ends by 10:00 the next day); bookable up to 12 months ahead; availability-limited ('je nach Verfuegbarkeit'). Super Sparpreis Young cannot be exchanged or cancelled except free of charge within 180 minutes of booking; Sparpreis Young costs EUR 10 to cancel before the first day (3-year voucher). Age is checked on board, so carry a passport. DB's pages set no residency requirement but do not explicitly address foreign visitors.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if any leg is inside Germany (e.g. Berlin-Hamburg or Berlin-Munich): book early for the lowest price, no card needed; no help for cross-border legs.
notes: Prices are 'from' prices and depend on train and date. DB's international Sparpreis Europa youth pricing was not checked.

provider: Deutsche Bahn - My BahnCard 25 (ages 6-26) and Probe BahnCard 25
ageRange: 6-26 for My BahnCard 25 (online order from age 18); Probe BahnCard 25 has no age limit
cost: My BahnCard 25: EUR 39.90 per year (2nd class), EUR 81.90 (1st class). Probe BahnCard 25: EUR 19.90 for 3 months (2nd class), EUR 39.90 (1st class).
benefit: 25% off Flexpreis and Sparpreis fares (including Super Sparpreis and the Young fares) for long-distance travel in Germany in the matching class; not on the City-Ticket.
typicalSaving: 25% of eligible fares; break-even is about EUR 160 of eligible fares for My BahnCard 25 and about EUR 80 for the Probe card, per traveller.
howToGet: Order on bahn.de or in DB Navigator (My BahnCard 25 online from 18) or at a DB Reisezentrum.
conditions: Both cards renew automatically for one year unless cancelled in text form at least 4 weeks before the term ends (the My BahnCard follow-up card becomes a full-price BahnCard at 27; follow-on price of the Probe card was not retrieved). The discount applies within Germany. DB's pages do not say whether people without a German address can buy the card online.
worthItForThisTrip: No: the EUR 19.90 Probe card only breaks even at about EUR 80 of eligible German fares per person and must be cancelled 4 weeks before it ends to avoid a one-year renewal.
notes: The Jugend BahnCard (EUR 7.90 per year, up to age 18) is for children and does not apply at 23.

provider: ÖBB (Austria) - Vorteilscard Jugend
ageRange: up to age 25 (buy until the day before the 26th birthday)
cost: EUR 21 per year (Vorteilscard Jugend); Vorteilscard Classic EUR 73
benefit: 50% off ÖBB standard (full-price) tickets for 12 months; photo ID proving age must be shown with the card.
typicalSaving: 50% of standard tickets; ÖBB states the card gives no discount on Sparschiene tickets.
howToGet: ÖBB app, ÖBB Ticketshop (shop.oebbtickets.at), ÖBB ticket counters or ÖBB sales partners.
conditions: Valid 12 months; renews automatically if a SEPA direct-debit mandate was given. ÖBB's pages state no residence or nationality requirement. ÖBB confirms the Vorteilscard does not reduce Sparschiene fares (Sparschiene Austria from EUR 9.90 in 2nd class; Sparschiene Europe from EUR 4.90 on short routes; non-refundable, limited availability).
worthItForThisTrip: No for a short trip: it only pays back after about EUR 42 of standard-fare tickets per person, while Sparschiene fares start at EUR 9.90 and get no card discount.
notes: Standard-fare levels for specific Austrian routes were not retrieved. Whether foreign residents can buy the Jugend card is not stated on the pages read. The Classic card (EUR 73) has no age limit.

provider: České dráhy (ČD, Czech Railways) - student fare 50%
ageRange: 18-25/26 (ČD title says 18-25, its text says 18-26; student IDs are issued until the day before the 26th birthday)
benefit: 50% off the regular fare in 2nd class (Flexi, Discounted Flexi, Fixed and route tickets) for domestic Czech journeys; accepted proof is a Czech pupil/student ID or a valid ISIC card.
typicalSaving: 50% of the regular domestic fare.
howToGet: Buy at a ČD ticket counter, in the e-shop or from the conductor (if the departure station's office was closed); show ISIC or student ID.
conditions: Domestic tickets only; on cross-border trains the national discount applies only up to the last Czech station (ISIC.cz). Not valid on intra-regional Os/Sp trains in the Zlin, Pilsen, South Moravian and Moravian-Silesian regions. ČD's page does not mention foreign students; ISIC.cz says eligibility includes students 'with a similar status abroad' but does not say that a foreign ISIC is accepted.
worthItForThisTrip: Only useful for domestic Czech hops such as Prague-Brno or Prague-Ostrava, and only if a Norwegian ISIC is accepted, which is unconfirmed (ČD info line +420 221 111 122, info@cd.cz).
notes: eligibleAt23 left null because the legal wording ('full-time study in the Czech Republic or similar status abroad') leaves foreign students ambiguous. Interrail One Country Pass for Czechia (EUR 79 for 3 days) is the alternative.

provider: RegioJet (trains) - student fare 50%
ageRange: 18-25 on the English tariff page, 18-26 on the Czech page
benefit: Student category: 50% discount on Low cost, Standard and Relax fares (2nd class, incl. berth and bed options) for full-time students with a valid international ISIC card (or Czech student card).
typicalSaving: 50% of the fare on the Czech part of the route.
howToGet: Choose the 'Student' passenger category when booking on regiojet.com or the app and show ISIC on board.
conditions: On international journeys the discount applies only to the part inside the Czech Republic (English tariff page; the Czech page says RegioJet deducts only the Czech share). Lists of students or enrolment confirmations are not accepted, only ISIC or a student card. Interrail passes are valid on RegioJet with a mandatory reservation of EUR 1.30-2.80.
worthItForThisTrip: Worth carrying ISIC for Prague-Brno / Prague-Ostrava style legs; for Prague-Vienna or Prague-Budapest only the Czech share is discounted, so expect modest savings.
notes: RegioJet pages are JavaScript-rendered and could not be opened by the fetch tool; wording comes from search results quoting regiojet.com and from the ISIC Czech Republic page. Third-party sites claim up to 51% or a 10% ISIC discount for over-26s; not used.

provider: RegioJet (buses) - student fare 50%
ageRange: 18-25/26 (see RegioJet trains)
benefit: Same 50% student category as on the trains (RegioJet's Czech discount page speaks of its yellow trains and buses); ISIC is the proof.
typicalSaving: 50% of the Czech share of the fare.
howToGet: Select the student passenger category on regiojet.com / app and carry ISIC.
conditions: Only the Czech Republic part of a journey is discounted; fare-class and age details as for RegioJet trains. The English tariff page did not clearly confirm bus coverage.
worthItForThisTrip: Marginal: a bus hop inside Czechia can be half price with ISIC, but international bus legs only get the Czech share discounted.
notes: Bus coverage rests on a search-result summary of the Czech page; not directly confirmed.

provider: PKP Intercity (Poland) - statutory student discount 51%
ageRange: students up to 26
benefit: 51% off 2nd class on all national PKP Intercity categories (EIP, EIC, IC, TLK).
typicalSaving: 51% for those who qualify; not available to a Norwegian visiting Poland.
howToGet: Not applicable to the group (qualifying students use a Polish e-student card).
conditions: Official table of documents: an electronic student card (mStudent) from a Polish higher-education institution; for students studying abroad, Polish citizens may use a Polish student card or ISIC, and EU citizens a Polish student card or ISIC together with a document proving a permanent-residence right in Poland. A Norwegian student with a Norwegian student ID or ISIC fits none of the listed categories (Norway is EEA/EFTA, not EU, and has no Polish residence right).
worthItForThisTrip: No - treat it as unavailable and compare PKP Intercity promo fares, the Interrail Poland pass (EUR 50 for 3 days) or other operators instead.
notes: The eligibility PDF is dated June 2021 in its metadata, but the current English offer page repeats the same categories. The discount is national-routes only.

provider: MÁV (Hungary) - young person discount 50% (ages 14-25)
benefit: 50% off discounted domestic tickets for 14-25-year-olds; proof is an ID document suitable for identification, regardless of citizenship (MAV Group discount table valid from 15 April 2026).
typicalSaving: 50% of the domestic fare.
howToGet: Buy a domestic ticket as a young person (14-25) and show passport or ID on request; the student card alone is not accepted as proof of age.
conditions: Domestic MAV services only (international tickets are priced separately, not verified). The 90% student pass discounts need a Hungarian student card and do not apply to visitors.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes for any purely Hungarian rail leg (e.g. Budapest to Gyor or Szeged); irrelevant for international legs such as Vienna-Budapest.
notes: Table text read from the official MAV discount PDF (Hungarian). The wording 'allampolgarsagtol fuggetlenul' means regardless of citizenship.

provider: Trenitalia - FrecciaYOUNG (CartaFRECCIA, under 30)
ageRange: under 30
cost: CartaFRECCIA is free; FrecciaYOUNG tickets have fixed fares of EUR 19, EUR 29 or EUR 39
benefit: Fixed low fares on Frecciarossa and Frecciargento in 2nd/Standard class for CartaFRECCIA members under 30.
howToGet: Register for the free CartaFRECCIA online, then choose the Young offer on trenitalia.com or the app.
conditions: Bookable with 11 days' advance; not changeable or refundable (optional tiRimborso refund add-on EUR 3); seats are limited per day and per train. The page does not say whether non-Italian residents are accepted or whether ID is checked on board (carry a passport anyway).
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Italy is on the route: EUR 19-39 for a Frecciarossa leg beats the Interrail Italy pass plus the EUR 13 reservation, but buy at least 11 days ahead (by 26 Nov for travel on 7 Dec).
notes: The regular fare for comparison was not retrieved. Young Intercity and Young Regionale offers exist but their conditions were not on the page.

provider: Italo - Italo Young (14-29)
benefit: 40% to 70% off the Flex fare in Smart class on Italo high-speed trains (and Italo plus Itabus tickets).
typicalSaving: 40-70% off the Flex fare.
howToGet: Search on italotreno.com or the app, select the number of travellers aged 14-29 and pick the Italo Young offer.
conditions: Buy at least 11 days before departure; can be modified until 72 hours before departure; non-refundable; subject to availability and only shown during booking if conditions are met; a valid ID may be requested on board. No Italian-residency or Italian-ID requirement is stated. Interrail passes are not valid on Italo (reported by third parties; Italo is not on Interrail's fee page).
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Italy is on the route: compare it with FrecciaYOUNG for each leg (Italo Young is changeable until 72 hours before departure).
notes: The discount is relative to the Flex fare, so the absolute price depends on route and date.

provider: Renfe (Spain) - Mas Renfe Joven card and Carne Joven
ageRange: 14-25 (age on the purchase date)
cost: Tarjeta Mas Renfe Joven: EUR 50 per year (renewal EUR 50)
benefit: 30% off the dynamic price on AVE, AVE International (Spain-France) and Larga Distancia; 25% off Avant, Media Distancia and Cercanias/Rodalies. The regional Carne Joven (separate card) gives 5% on AVE/Larga Distancia and 20% on Avant, Media Distancia and Feve; Renfe's page says EYCA, ISIC, IYTC and GO 25 cards are also valid for the Carne Joven discounts.
typicalSaving: 30% / 25% off the fare; break-even is about EUR 167 of AVE/Larga Distancia fares per person.
howToGet: Buy online at renfe.com (bank card or Renfe Points); you receive a customer number and a PDF or Passbook card.
conditions: Not valid on AVLO, tourist trains or Cercanias Ancho Metrico; cannot be combined with other discounts except Familia Numerosa; the card is not a ticket; valid one year; the conditions page states no residence, nationality or ID requirement. The summer 'Verano Joven' scheme (50% on high-speed, max EUR 30 per ticket) ended 30 Sep 2026 and required Spanish nationality, or EU nationality with legal residence in Spain (per Renfe).
worthItForThisTrip: Unlikely: EUR 50 per person only pays back after about EUR 167 of full AVE/Larga Distancia fares, and 5 friends would each need a card.
notes: Whether an ISIC or EYCA actually earns the Carne Joven percentages for non-Spaniards is ambiguous on the Renfe page.

provider: Iryo and Ouigo Espana - youth fares
benefit: No standing youth or student fare found at either operator; the only youth schemes were the government 'Verano Joven' summer discounts (1 Jul-30 Sep 2026, ages 18-30, Spanish nationality or legal residence required, already ended).
howToGet: Not applicable.
conditions: Ouigo had an extra 10% on top of Verano Joven and a 50% autumn voucher tied to summer purchases (not obtainable now). Ouigo offers a discount code to members of the Spanish youth hostel network (REAJ) via the network; details not verified.
worthItForThisTrip: No youth discount to claim; simply compare the operators' advance fares.
notes: Negative finding based on the operators' official promotion pages as shown in search results; the pages were not fetched individually.

provider: SNCF (France) - Carte Avantage Jeune
ageRange: 12-27 (valid until the day before the 28th birthday)
benefit: 30% off TGV INOUI and Intercites all year (not OUIGO); also 30% on TGV INOUI to Luxembourg and Italy, to Germany (TGV INOUI and DB-SNCF), TGV Lyria to Switzerland, TGV INOUI to Spain and TGV France-Brussels. Capped 2nd class fares inside France: EUR 49 for journeys under 1h30, EUR 69 for 1h30-3h, EUR 89 over 3h. Access to last-minute NO FLEX offers.
typicalSaving: 30% off fares; break-even is about EUR 163 of full-price tickets per person.
howToGet: Buy on SNCF Connect (PDF card by email, e-card option); choose the start date up to 5 months after purchase.
conditions: Card is personal; withdrawal within 14 days if no discount was used; exchange/refund free until 7 days before departure, then EUR 19 per person per journey on TGV INOUI. No residence, address or ID requirement is stated on the page read.
worthItForThisTrip: Unlikely: each traveller would need roughly EUR 163 of full-price TGV tickets to repay the EUR 49 card (EUR 245 for five), so only consider it if several long French TGV legs are planned.
notes: One snippet says the price applies from 1 Jan 2026, the SNCF Connect page says from 1 Jul 2024; the price is EUR 49 in both. Third-party 39 EUR deals were limited campaigns that ended.

provider: NS (Netherlands) - youth fares on international tickets
ageRange: up to 25 (some pages say under 26; EuroCity up to 26)
benefit: NS International sells youth fares: 30% off 2nd class on regional trains via Maastricht or Roosendaal, youth fares on Eurostar, and an extra youth discount (up to age 26) on EuroCity / EuroCity Direct trains. No domestic youth discount for visitors was found; the student travel product (40% or 100% off the Dutch leg of an international ticket) needs an NS student travel product on an OV-chipkaart.
typicalSaving: 30% on the regional cross-border routes named; other routes list no percentage.
howToGet: Book on nsinternational.com and change 'Adult (26 to 59)' to 'Young person'; youth fares do not show in the price calendar and can only be booked online.
conditions: Youth fares on Eurostar are subject to availability; the pages do not say whether non-Dutch nationals qualify (the youth category is age-based).
worthItForThisTrip: Only if Amsterdam or Brussels is a stop and the leg is booked as an international NS ticket; nothing to claim for travel inside the Netherlands.
notes: NS pages are inconsistent on the age limit (25 vs 26). The Student Mobility Card (EUR 15, 15% off-peak) is for enrolled international students in the Netherlands, not visitors.

provider: Eurostar - youth fare
ageRange: 12-25 inclusive on the day of travel
benefit: Up to 20% off the adult price in Eurostar Standard and up to 15% off in Plus and Premier, on routes between France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany.
typicalSaving: Up to 20% (Standard) / 15% (Plus, Premier).
howToGet: Search for one-way trips on eurostar.com and look for the youth fare in the fare options.
conditions: Subject to availability and on certain trains only; one-way trips only; the page mentions no ID, nationality or residency rule. The page lists the age range as 12-25 although the headline says 'under 26'. Whether London routes carry the same youth fare could not be checked (UK page returned an error).
worthItForThisTrip: Only if the route includes a Paris/Brussels/Amsterdam/Cologne Eurostar leg; the saving is a modest percentage and availability is limited.
notes: Only the US-site version of the page could be read.

provider: FlixBus
ageRange: 18-26 (Czech domestic student fare only)
benefit: No general youth or student reduction found on FlixBus's official discount pages. Country exceptions seen: Czechia - 50% for full-time students 18-26 on domestic Czech routes (ISIC or Czech student card; the page says 'within the whole EU'); Denmark - reduced prices for students, children and pensioners on domestic trips with photo ID.
typicalSaving: 50% on domestic Czech routes only.
howToGet: Czechia: choose the passenger category 'Studenti - do 26 let' when booking and show a valid card to the driver.
conditions: Czech discount is domestic only; whether a Norwegian (EEA, not EU) ISIC holder qualifies is not stated. FlixBus's Black Friday sale cannot be combined with student discounts. Some third-party sites mention Student Beans / UNiDAYS codes of about 10%; unverified.
worthItForThisTrip: Assume full FlixBus prices for international hops; the only reliable cut is the Czech domestic student fare.
notes: FlixBus's global discount page covers Poland's statutory discounts only (none for 23-year-olds). The Czech page title says 60% but its body says 50%.

provider: Ecolines
ageRange: 13-18 with ISIC (teen category)
benefit: No youth or student fare for a 23-year-old found; the only ISIC-based category is for teens aged 13-18.
howToGet: Not applicable.
conditions: Discounted tickets require proof during the ride; Ecolines has a loyalty programme (eco-bonuses on some routes).
worthItForThisTrip: Nothing to claim - treat Ecolines fares as full price.
notes: Ecolines pages are JavaScript-rendered; the finding comes from search-result summaries of its terms pages, some of which look old.

provider: Hostelling International membership (HI Norge)
ageRange: no age limit stated for HI Norge (DJH Germany: junior fee up to 26)
cost: NOK 50 per year for HI Norge membership (about EUR 4.7 at the project's fx rate of 10.7155 NOK/EUR); price from a Visit Norway listing and a search snippet of HI Norge's page, not visible in the page text we could read
benefit: HI Norge advertises 10% off accommodation plus all international HI discounts; HI membership gives member rates at HI hostels worldwide or a discount on non-member rates. Germany (DJH) hostels are members-only: non-members need a Guest Card (EUR 3.50 per night stamp, or EUR 18 for an immediate international card), and the EUR 6 per night surcharge applies only to guests aged 27 or over, not to 23-year-olds.
typicalSaving: About 10% of the room price; in German DJH hostels about EUR 3.50 per night versus the Guest Card.
howToGet: Join through the HI Norge member portal (hihostels.app) for a digital card before departure; HI requires the membership to be bought in your country of residence.
conditions: Local conditions apply: in some countries membership is compulsory, discount sizes differ, and some benefits need membership of the local association. HI Norge's discount is reported to apply when booking via hihostels.no or directly with the hostel. DJH says membership of any other national Youth Hostel Association is enough, but confirm with the hostel. Whether the discount applies to private rooms was not stated.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if any nights are in HI/DJH hostel private rooms, since NOK 50 is repaid within a night or two (10% rate or avoiding German Guest Card stamps); otherwise skip.
notes: The NOK 50 price rests on two soft sources (Visit Norway listing and a search snippet of HI Norge's membership page). Interrail's pass-benefits page names Hostelworld as a partner but lists no discount. Which cities on the route have HI hostels with private rooms was not checked.

provider: a&o Hostels - student rate, ISIC and rail-pass discounts
benefit: Student offer through the free a&o Club: 20% off Fixed bookings or 10% off the Flex rate. An a&o press release (circa 2017) says ISIC holders get 10% off the daily rate at all locations plus a free soft drink. The German a&o page offers 10% off each night to holders of German, InterRail or Eurail rail passes.
typicalSaving: 10-20% of the room price.
howToGet: Register for the a&o Club, log in and book directly on aohostels.com; show ISIC at reception for the older ISIC offer.
conditions: Student page does not mention proof of student status; the rail-pass claim procedure and the locations covered were not retrieved; the ISIC press release is not dated and may be outdated.
worthItForThisTrip: Worth checking for hostel private rooms in a&o cities because membership is free and no ISIC is needed for the club rate, but compare the final price with apartments and Hostelworld first.
notes: a&o's rail-pass discount page did not load usable text; the 10% figure is from the German youth-hotels page.

provider: Generator Hostels - ISIC promo code
benefit: ISIC cardholders can get a promo code for 20% off the Pay Later rate on the Generator website (listing on ISIC Portugal); other ISIC country sites show different codes.
typicalSaving: Up to 20% of the Pay Later rate.
howToGet: Request the code through the ISIC discount listing, then book on generatorhostels.com.
conditions: Bookings must be guaranteed by credit card and cannot be cancelled; an ISIC/EYCA card may be requested on arrival and the booking cancelled if not shown; the code differs by ISIC country and was not found on isic.no.
worthItForThisTrip: Probably not worth chasing: unverified for Norwegian ISIC holders and the rate is non-cancellable.
notes: Pages could not be opened directly; details come from search-result summaries of the ISIC Portugal and Romania listings.

provider: Airbnb, Booking.com and Hostelworld - youth/student deals
benefit: No youth or student discount found. Booking.com has no student programme (its free Genius loyalty tiers depend on stay history, 10% at entry to 20% at the top, per a third-party guide); Hostelworld has no verified student or under-26 discount; nothing was found for Airbnb.
howToGet: Not applicable.
conditions: Student Beans or UNiDAYS listings for Booking.com and Hostelworld (around 8-10%) appear on third-party pages but could not be verified.
worthItForThisTrip: Nothing to claim - budget at list price and use HI, a&o or Interrail partner offers where applicable.
notes: Only third-party sources were available (the fetch tool could not open these companies' own help pages in this session), so this is an absence-of-evidence finding.

provider: ISIC (International Student Identity Card) - Norway
ageRange: 12 and over, no upper age limit (full-time students)
cost: NOK 100 for the digital ISIC (valid 12 months, in the ISIC app); about EUR 9.3 at the project's fx rate of 10.7155 NOK/EUR. The isic.no eligibility text also mentions EUR 10.
benefit: Accepted student proof at Vy, SJ Norge (international students) and SJ Sweden; domestic Czech student fares (CD, RegioJet, FlixBus CZ); recommended for foreign students at Museo Reina Sofia; reduced student prices at Museo Thyssen and National Gallery Prague; KILROY flight offers (up to EUR 35 off); a&o and Generator hostel offers (see those entries).
howToGet: Order at isic.no ('Bestill ISIC-kortet'), document full-time student status (at least 15 hours per week for 12 weeks per year; a Norwegian university page says a student-status confirmation from Studentweb works), then activate the card in the ISIC app.
conditions: Full-time students at an approved institution; physical card option not confirmed on isic.no. Most big savings in this file (Louvre, Colosseum, Portugal, MAV, Interrail, FrecciaYOUNG, Italo Young, Avantage Jeune) are age-based and need only a passport or ID, not ISIC.
worthItForThisTrip: A cheap hedge at about EUR 9 per person: it pays for itself on a single Czech domestic half-price fare, a Reina Sofia visit or a reduced Prague gallery entry, but skip it if the route avoids Czechia and Spain.
notes: Price per isic.no and a HVL (university) page. The IYTC youth card (under 30, non-students) and the EYCA European Youth Card appear on several museum pages as alternatives; their price and availability for Norwegians were not checked.

provider: France - Louvre, Musee d'Orsay and national museums (under-26 EEA free entry)
ageRange: under 26 (ministry wording 18-25; under 18 free for everyone)
benefit: Louvre: free for EEA citizens under 26 with valid photo ID, or EEA residents under 26 with photo ID plus a residence permit valid for over 90 days (the EEA list includes Norway). Ministry of Culture: permanent collections of national museums are free for 18-25-year-olds who reside regularly in an EU or EEA state. Musee d'Orsay lists under-26 EEA residents as free. Versailles: under-26 EU/EEA residents free per a third-party guide, with a free timed slot required.
typicalSaving: EUR 22 per person for the Louvre alone (standard EEA ticket; EUR 32 for non-EEA visitors).
howToGet: No card needed: carry passport or national ID; the Louvre recommends booking a free time slot online; Orsay free entry is claimed with proof at the entrance; Versailles needs a free reserved slot.
conditions: The ministry rule covers permanent collections (temporary exhibitions may be charged; not stated for under-26s); ID is checked at the entrance. The Louvre is free for everyone on the first Friday of the month after 18:00 (not July/August), which is 4 Dec 2026, just before the trip.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes - if Paris is a stop this is the biggest single saving (about EUR 22 per person at the Louvre alone, more with Orsay and Versailles) at no cost.
notes: Louvre and ministry pages were read directly. The Orsay billetterie page returned 403, so its rule is from a search summary; Versailles rests on a third-party guide (official site not reachable).

provider: Italy - state museums and archaeological sites (Colosseum, Herculaneum, Uffizi etc.)
ageRange: 18-25 reduced (until the day of the 25th birthday); under 18 free
benefit: EU citizens aged 18-25 pay a reduced EUR 2 ticket at the Colosseum Archaeological Park and other state sites (Herculaneum: EUR 2 reduced vs EUR 16 full). The official Colosseo page applies the free/reduced provisions of Ministerial Decree 239/2006 to citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland (EEA) without stating the amount.
typicalSaving: Herculaneum EUR 14 off (EUR 16 to EUR 2); the Colosseum reduced price is EUR 2 against a full price of up to EUR 24 for the Full Experience ticket.
howToGet: Carry passport or ID; at the Colosseum Park the reduced and free tickets must be booked on ticketing.colosseo.it or bought at the ticket offices.
conditions: The CoopCulture (Herculaneum) and Colosseo pages speak of EU citizens; Norway is covered only via the Colosseo line on EEA nationals, so confirm at the ticket office. The first Sunday of each month is free for all (6 Dec 2026, the day before the trip).
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Rome, Naples/Pompeii or Florence are stops: EUR 2 entry at major state sites is a large saving for an ID check.
notes: The Colosseum Full Experience price (EUR 24) is from a search-result summary of the official site. Uffizi and other Italian state museums follow the same ministry decree but their pages were not opened.

provider: Spain - Museo Reina Sofia and Museo del Prado (students 18-25)
ageRange: students 18-25 (also under 18 free)
benefit: Museo Reina Sofia: free entry for students aged 18-25 in any degree (no nationality condition; foreign students advised to bring an ISIC), and for holders of a carne joven or equivalent. Museo del Prado: free entry for students aged 18-25 per its price page (as quoted in search results) and 50% off for EYCA/IYTC holders. Museo Thyssen: reduced (not free) price for students with a student card or ISIC, free for carne joven holders.
howToGet: Collect the free-with-accreditation ticket at the ticket office on the day, showing the accreditation document (with expiry date, Latin script or certified translation) together with passport or ID.
conditions: Free tickets with accreditation are only available at the ticket office. Reina Sofia is also free in the last two hours before closing (online reservation) and on free days (6 Dec 2026, before the trip). Prado conditions come from search snippets because the official page returned 403.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Madrid is a stop: bring a student certificate/ISIC and passport for free Reina Sofia (and likely Prado) entry.
notes: General admission prices were not retrieved, so no euro saving is stated. An announcement of a EUR 3 Alhambra price for young Europeans with the European Youth Card was seen in one snippet but is unverified.

provider: Greece - archaeological sites and museums (Acropolis etc.)
ageRange: 6-25 (EU youth up to 25 free; non-EU youth 6-25 at 50%)
benefit: EU citizens up to 25 enter free with ID card or passport; youth 6-25 from outside the EU pay 50% from 1 April to 31 October with a passport; from 1 November to 31 March every visitor gets a 50% reduced ticket, so in December the group pays half price at least.
typicalSaving: 50% in December (all visitors); free entry only if Greece treats Norwegians as EU youth, which is unconfirmed.
howToGet: Show passport or ID at the ticket desk; timed-entry slots apply at major Athens sites per third-party guides.
conditions: The rule text names 'member states of the European Union' for free entry and 'countries outside the European Union' for the 50% rate; Norway is EEA but not EU and is not mentioned. Free days: first Sunday of each month from 1 Nov to 31 Mar (6 Dec 2026, before the trip), 28 Oct, 18 Apr, 18 May, 6 Mar and the last weekend of September.
worthItForThisTrip: Only if Athens is a stop: expect the winter 50% rate rather than free entry unless the ticket office accepts EEA youth as EU youth.
notes: Rules read from the EU Eurydice page quoting the Greek ministry (updated March 2026); the ministry page itself returned 403. Actual ticket prices were not retrieved.

provider: Portugal - Museus e Monumentos de Portugal (Jeronimos, Belem Tower etc.)
ageRange: 13-24 inclusive
benefit: 50% off the regular ticket for visitors aged 13 to 24 inclusive; no nationality or residency condition is stated. Children up to 12 are free; residents of Portugal get 52 free days per year with the citizen card.
typicalSaving: Jeronimos Monastery EUR 18 to EUR 9; Belem Tower EUR 15 to EUR 7.50 (50% of the listed prices).
howToGet: Show passport or ID at the ticket office or validation point; free tickets and discounts require a valid official document.
conditions: The page does not list which documents prove age; 'unemployed visitors residing in the EU' and teachers/students on study visits have separate free categories.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Lisbon is a stop: about EUR 16.50 saved for Jeronimos plus Belem Tower, at no cost.
notes: Prices shown on the official tickets page on the date of checking.

provider: Germany - Staatliche Museen zu Berlin (Museum Island etc.)
ageRange: under 18 free; students any age at 50%
benefit: 50% reduced admission for pupils, trainees and students (with a certificate); free admission up to the 18th birthday. The page has no rule for visitors under 26 or for EU/EEA residents and does not mention ISIC or foreign student IDs.
typicalSaving: 50% of the full ticket price (prices not retrieved).
howToGet: Show a student certificate at the entrance without being asked.
conditions: University students are free only in registered groups attending courses. No German-wide EU under-26 scheme was found; other Berlin and Dresden museums set their own rules.
worthItForThisTrip: Modest: only a 50% student reduction (bring a student certificate), no free entry for 23-year-olds.
notes: Germany has no equivalent of the French/Spanish under-26 freebies in sources found; the first-Sunday 'Museumssonntag' (6 Dec 2026) is before the trip.

provider: Czechia - National Gallery Prague (and Prague Castle)
ageRange: 16-26 (reduced); under 15 free
benefit: National Gallery Prague long-term collections: reduced admission for young people aged 16 to 26 and for students with a valid ISIC; free for children under 15. Prague Castle Main Circuit: reduced CZK 300 against a basic CZK 450 for students up to 26 with ID, per third-party guides.
typicalSaving: Prague Castle about CZK 150 per person (third-party figures); the Gallery's reduced percentage was not stated.
howToGet: Show passport or student ID/ISIC at the ticket desk.
conditions: The gallery page mentions no nationality or residency requirement; the two reduced categories appear with typos on the page. Prague Castle student rules were not confirmed on hrad.cz.
worthItForThisTrip: Modest: reduced prices of roughly one third off at Prague Castle if Prague is a stop; carry ISIC to be safe.
notes: Prague Castle's own site returned 403; figures are from third-party guides. Older sources said the Gallery's permanent collection is free for everyone under 26 (Komerční banka sponsorship from 2015); the current page lists reduced admission instead.

provider: Poland - National Museum in Warsaw (and Wawel Royal Castle)
ageRange: students under 26
benefit: National Museum in Warsaw: 1 PLN ticket for children, teenagers and students under 26 (ticket office only); permanent galleries free on Tuesdays; regular ticket 30 PLN, reduced 15 PLN; 50% off all tickets on Fridays 17:00-20:00 (not on 1 PLN tickets). Wawel Royal Castle: reduced tickets for young people up to 26 with a valid student ID (third-party, EYCA also listed).
typicalSaving: 29 PLN per person against the regular permanent-gallery ticket (30 PLN), or free on a Tuesday.
howToGet: Buy the 1 PLN ticket at the museum ticket office showing student ID or ISIC; Tuesdays need no ticket for the permanent exhibition.
conditions: The page does not say whether proof is required or whether foreign students qualify, and does not mention ISIC; the Tuesday free admission excludes temporary exhibitions. Tuesdays inside the trip window: 8 Dec and 15 Dec 2026.
worthItForThisTrip: Yes if Warsaw is a stop: free permanent galleries on Tuesday 8 or 15 Dec, or 1 PLN with a student card on other days.
notes: National Museum figures come from the official page; Wawel's own page returned 404, so its youth rule is third-party and unverified.

provider: Austria - Belvedere and federal museums (Vienna)
ageRange: students under 26; children and youth under 19 free
benefit: Belvedere: students under 26 pay EUR 19 for the Upper Belvedere (standard EUR 23), EUR 16 for the Lower Belvedere (EUR 20) and EUR 8 for Belvedere 21 (EUR 12); under-19s free. Albertina and Kunsthistorisches Museum are also free for under-19s (third-party sources).
typicalSaving: EUR 4 per person per Belvedere site.
howToGet: Choose the student price at the ticket desk or online and show a student ID.
conditions: The page does not state which proof is required. At 23 the group gets only student prices, not free entry; no student rate for the KHM or Albertina was confirmed.
worthItForThisTrip: Small: about EUR 4 off per Belvedere ticket with a student ID.
notes: Search for KHM and Albertina student rates was not possible after the web-search budget ran out; check khm.at and albertina.at.

provider: Hungary - Hungarian National Museum and National Gallery (Budapest)
ageRange: 6-26 for the youth ticket; EEA citizens under 26 for the free day
benefit: Hungarian National Museum: youth ticket 1,750 HUF for Hungarian and EEA citizens aged 6-26 (adult 3,500 HUF); permanent exhibitions free on the third Saturday of each month for EEA citizens under 26; free for everyone on 15 March, 20 August and 23 October. Hungarian National Gallery: 50% discount for EEA citizens aged 6-26 (search summary of the official site).
typicalSaving: 1,750 HUF per person (50% of the adult ticket).
howToGet: Show passport or ID with photo plus proof of eligibility at the ticket desk.
conditions: The free third-Saturday in December 2026 is 19 Dec, after the trip window (Saturday 12 Dec is the second Saturday); the discount requires a photo ID or passport.
worthItForThisTrip: Modest: half-price tickets (1,750 HUF) at the National Museum if Budapest is a stop; the free day falls outside 7-15 Dec.
notes: National Museum prices and rules read from the official page; the National Gallery page returned a server error, so its 50% figure comes from a search summary.
